messages:
mia: quick heads-up — canary deploy #476 bumped p99 by ~60ms for short sequences after the kernel selector tweak yesterday. not sure if admit logic or kv behavior is the root cause. :thinking:

devin: saw that in dashboards. latency spike aligns with a KV cold-hit burst around 09:23 UTC. small requests (<=64 tokens) show largest regression.

sanjay: throwing a profiler snapshot here — flame output clipped: 
```
p50: 12ms  p95: 45ms  p99: 210ms
kernel_copy_kv: 35ms (hot)  80ms (miss)
batch_pack: 6ms
queue_admit_check: 18ms (high variance)
```

lina: interesting that queue_admit_check is noisy. could be token_budget drifting so small-seq requests get queued behind long ones and then kernel swap happens.

mia: I replayed a trace — many short requests end up in mixed batches with long contexts after recent batching heuristic change (prefer kernel affinity over length affinity). that increases kv eviction churn.

devin: here's a short diff of the admit config we rolled: 
```
admit: {
  mode: "kernel_affinity_first",
  token_budget_target: 0.85,
  seq_length_weight: 1.0,
  reserve_for_short: 0
}
```

sanjay: propose an experiment: reintroduce a tiny short-seq reserve (n=6 slots) and lower token_budget_target to 0.7 for canary pool. aim: keep small requests forming short-only microbatches and reduce KV churn.

lina: +1. also add a KV-hit guard: if recent kv_miss_rate > 12% then prefer length_affinity for next 30s. simple thresholding can dodge cold bursts.

mia: agreed. devin can you schedule canary? runtime-bot do the deploy and profile capture? @runtime-bot

runtime-bot: deploy queued: canary pool shard-c2 -> admit-config v2. ETA 2m. Starting profiler sampling for 10m. :rocket:

profile-bot: initial baseline metrics attached: 
- baseline p99 short-req: 180ms
- baseline kv_miss_rate: 3.8%
- baseline batch_size_mean(short): 3.2

devin: deploying config patch now: 
```
admit: {
  mode: "hybrid",
  token_budget_target: 0.70,
  seq_length_weight: 0.8,
  reserve_for_short: 6,
  kv_miss_guard: {
    enable: true,
    threshold: 0.12,
    fallback: "length_affinity",
    window_sec: 30
  }
}
```

mia: after 5m of traffic: p99 for short down to 125ms, kv_miss spikes absorbed, batch_size_mean(short) -> 5.1 (better packing), overall cpu kernel_switch counts down ~40%. :tada:

sanjay: nice. one caveat — some mid-length requests (200-400 tokens) saw slight p50 increase (~8ms) due to reserve. acceptable trade for now.

lina: let's run A/B for 24h and capture per-model kernel choice histogram + token_budget utilization. If we see oscillation, we should add hysteresis on kv_miss_guard (eg 3-sample majority).

mia: action items: 1) devex to add canary config doc + ribbon for toggling reserve (devin) 2) add hysteresis to kv_miss_guard (sanjay) 3) perf team to produce per-second kernel switch metric (lina). I'll open tickets.

devin: creating ticket INF-981: "canary admit v2: short-reserve & kv-guard experiment" with logs + profiler link.

profile-bot: final 10m snapshot: p99 short-req: 118ms, kv_miss_rate: 4.5%, token_budget_util: 0.68, kernel_switch_rate: -38% vs baseline. attaching flamegraph link: https://internal/prof/476/flame.svg

mia: great. leaving canary running. if A/B holds we'll roll to more shards tomorrow. thanks all. :thumbsup:
